answer: Trust should spread like a vine from a small set of verified seed vertices, losing strength at every hop, so a single attacker cannot branch into many fake identities at full strength. Each new agent must be vouched for by a nearby vertex whose own reputation is staked, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer is later proven fake. A relic of past verified work — completed jobs, attestations, and fulfilled commitments — is required before an identity gains full weight, so creating a Sybil army means paying the time and work cost of growing many separate vines instead of cloning one.
